episodes.title: Why We Study Art
episodes.description: In this episode of Crash Course Art History, we’ll learn how interpreting artwork reveals connections among all of us, across cultures and across time.

episodes.title: How to Look at Art
episodes.description: Learn terms for examining artwork and explore how its time and place influence its meaning.

episodes.title: The History of Museums
episodes.description: In this episode of Crash Course Art History, we’ll learn why museums are so much more than just collections of interesting and pretty objects.

episodes.title: What Makes an Artist “Great”?
episodes.description: We’ll learn about where the myth of the Great Artist comes from — and why it might be time for a new perspective.

episodes.title: Should We Separate Art from the Artist?
episodes.description: We’ll keep digging into the myth of the Great Artist, with whether we can—or should—separate artists’ personal actions and beliefs from the art they create.

episodes.title: What Makes Art “Good”?
episodes.description: Explore how culture, history, society, and storytelling shape evaluations of art beyond its price.

episodes.title: How Art Tells Stories
episodes.description: We discover that visual storytelling is elementally human — and so is competing over whose story is told.

episodes.title: What Counts as Religious Art?
episodes.description: In this episode, we’ll explore how concepts of the divine and spirituality intersect with the history of art.

episodes.title: The Hidden Meanings in Nature Art
episodes.description: We’ll learn about the ways artists use nature to make arguments about the world around us, and our place within it.

episodes.title: How Communities Make Art
episodes.description: In this episode we’ll learn how community is created through art.

episodes.title: Bodies in Art
episodes.description: We’ll learn what portraits and self-portraits can tell us about the people they represent and about artists who’ve used bodies to critique their societies.

episodes.title: Art’s History of Trade & Exchange
episodes.description: We’ll explore how trade networks have moved both materials and ideas — and how art reflects a multi-directional flow of influences.

episodes.title: Who Gets to Be a “Real” Artist? (Amateur & Outsider Art)
episodes.description: Explore amateur and outsider artists and how the boundaries of recognized art have shifted over time.

episodes.title: What’s the Difference Between Art & Design?
episodes.description: Explore the historical boundary between art and design through materials, techniques, fashion, and everyday objects.

episodes.title: What Even is Modern Art?
episodes.description: Our cultural perspectives shape how we perceive art, including who we see as contributing to its most important movements.

episodes.title: Why Is Everyone So Mad About Public Art?
episodes.description: We’ll learn about public art’s diversity of media, how it shapes collective identity, and why it seems to cause such intense controversy.

episodes.title: When Art is Illegal: Graffiti & Street Art
episodes.description: In this episode of Crash Course Art History, we’ll explore the various ways artists have used illicit public art to express themselves.

episodes.title: Is AI-Generated Art Original? (Authenticity & Originality)
episodes.description: We grapple with questions about artistic originality and authenticity that have plagued the art world for hundreds of years.

episodes.title: Why Is Art So Expensive?
episodes.description: Explore the history of the art market, how artworks acquire financial value, and its connections to imperialism.

episodes.title: When Art Meets Activism
episodes.description: Explore iconoclasm, protest art, and artists' encounters with authorities when challenging power.

episodes.title: The Importance of Preserving, Restoring, & Conserving Art
episodes.description: We’ll learn how art historians preserve, restore, and conserve art that tells the story of who we are and who we want to be.

episodes.title: What is the Future of Art?
episodes.description: In this episode of Crash Course Art History, we’ll learn how technology is shifting the ways we think about art’s past, present, and future.
